title: Andreeva routs Shnaider 6-2, 6-1, moves on to semifinals at season-ending WTA Finals

 Updated Nov. 13, 2026 4:42 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Associated Press INDIAN WELLS, Calif. (AP) — Mirra Andreeva won 12 of the final 13 games to cruise past Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 and complete her round-robin play at the WTA Finals on Friday.
 Andreeva dropped just 11 games total while winning Group 2 with a 3-0 record and will play Jessica Pegula in Saturday's semifinals. Either Aryna Sabalenka or Elina Svitolina , who meet later, will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the other semifinal at Indian Wells Tennis Garden.
 Shnaider, the second alternate, was a late replacement for Karolina Muchova , who withdrew with a gastrointestinal illness. Shnaider made her WTA Finals debut in singles after qualifying in doubles last year with fellow Russian Andreeva. They went 0-3 in round-robin play a year ago.
 Shnaider led 2-0 in the first set before Andreeva took control and wrapped up the win in 55 minutes. Andreeva won 71% of her first-serve points and converted six of seven break points. Shnaider committed 32 errors in her only match after spending the week practicing and not knowing whether she would be needed.
 “I don’t know how much fun that was,” Andreeva said. “It’s nice to share a court with your friend. It’s more nerve-wracking for me personally because I know her well.”
 Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, needed just over an hour to win her first two matches. The wind picked up considerably on Friday under sunny skies.
 “It was a little chaotic on the court,” she said.
 Muchova, a Wimbledon finalist this year, already lost her first two matches and could not have advanced to the semifinals even if she had played Friday. 
 Muchova is the second withdrawal of the eight-day, $10 million event. Top-ranked Elena Rybakina dropped out before the tournament began last Sunday, citing a viral illness and exhaustion.
 It's the first time since 2019 that both singles alternates are competing in the round-robin stage. Marta Kostyuk replaced Rybakina and she went 0-3 in Group 1 play.
